page: Amazon Web Services r8i.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing the Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8i.8xlarge demonstrates strong performance in text processing, placing in the top tier (top 10%) of Geekbench tests. Single-threaded gzip compression and both single- and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression benchmarks register in the top 25%. General CPU performance is also strong, with Passmark CPU and encryption scores reaching the top 25%, while Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores align with this tier. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks registers at 133.67 GB/sec for reads and 63.0 GB/sec for writes, placing in the middle 50% of tested systems.

This hardware configuration is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and text processing tasks. It also supports small-scale machine learning tasks; LLM text generation using a small 135M model ranks in the top 10% (404.39 tokens/sec), and prompt processing for a medium 7B model ranks in the top 25%. However, a notable performance tradeoff occurs with larger models, where text generation speed for a 70B model falls into the bottom 25% (2.71 tokens/sec) due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. The high-density DDR5 memory and dedicated Intel Xeon cores offer qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound enterprise applications that do not require local NVMe storage.
